facts.fact: In the MOU signed with the United States on 9 December 2025, Liberia commits to develop and use an open-source EMR as its individual patient information system in clinics, health centers and hospitals, interoperable with DHIS2, rolled out to 20% of all public health facilities in 2026, 60% in 2027, 80% in 2028, 90% in 2029 and 100% in 2030; these are targets, not achieved coverage.

The MOU plans US Government funding of US$2,676,744 for Electronic Medical Records systems over 2026-2030, of which US$827,050 in 2026, subject to availability of funds; Liberia commits to pay licensing, cloud and hardware costs the US does not, with no figure or budget line given.

In the MOU of 9 December 2025 Liberia commits to use HMIS/DHIS2 as its national integrated health data warehouse through 2030, with planned US support for equipment, training, server management and hosting, maintenance and upgrade, staffing and internet.

The MOU plans US Government funding of US$1,338,372 for HMIS/DHIS2 as the national health data warehouse over 2026-2030, of which US$413,525 in 2026, subject to availability of funds; Liberia commits to pay remaining licensing, cloud and hardware costs, with no figure or budget line given.
